answer: Total unrestricted inventory value is about USD 2,767,451.83. 5 of 1,160 stock rows have no moving average price, so they are left out of this figure.
how_calculated: SUM(LABST * VERPR) over ZV_STOCK (1,160 rows, one per material/plant/storage location/batch, no duplicates). A second check that summed by plant first gave the same total.
assumptions: ZV_STOCK is the live stock table. ZV_STOCK_BAK_2024 is a backup with different quantities and ZV_STOCK_TEST is a 200-row test subset. The ZCO_/ZFI_/ZMM_ etc. tables use different material and plant codes (M45, P1) and do not match the master data. Everything is in USD. VERPR is taken as the price per one base unit, because there is no price-unit column. 5 rows have no price and are excluded: 3218000006@2100, 1111000015@2100 (2 batches), 3114000070@1100 and 1120000076@2100. Only unrestricted stock (LABST) exists in the table.

answer: 585 distinct materials have stock on hand.
how_calculated: COUNT(DISTINCT MATNR) over ZV_STOCK, checked again with WHERE LABST > 0 (every row is positive).
assumptions: 'Different items' means distinct material numbers across all plants, not material-plant combinations. ZV_STOCK is the live table.

answer: Finished goods (material type FINISHED) are worth about USD 141,350.19 in unrestricted stock.
how_calculated: SUM(LABST * VERPR) over ZV_STOCK joined to ZV_MATERIAL on MATNR, filtered to MTART = 'FINISHED'. That is 87 rows with no missing prices. The breakdown by plant matches: 1110 72,260.51 + 2110 31,995.22 + 3100 37,094.46.
assumptions: 'Finished goods' means material type FINISHED. Another reading is stock held at the plants named 'Finished Goods' (1110 and 2110). Those plants also hold SEMI materials, so that reading gives a different total. USD only, priced per base unit.

answer: 80 material-plant combinations are below their reorder point.
how_calculated: Unrestricted stock in ZV_STOCK was summed by MATNR and WERKS, then left-joined from ZV_REORDER (818 unique material-plant rows). The count is where the stock (0 if there is none) is less than MINBE. 28 of the 80 have no stock at all. A further 71 sit exactly at the reorder point and are not counted.
assumptions: A warehouse is a plant (WERKS). The reorder level is MINBE, the reorder point, not safety stock (31 combinations are below safety stock). 'Below' means strictly less than. Only unrestricted stock is counted.

answer: 25 distinct lots with stock on hand have already expired.
how_calculated: Batches in ZV_STOCK with LABST > 0 (329 distinct) were joined to ZV_BATCH on CHARG. All of them match, and the material and plant agree. The count is distinct CHARG with VFDAT before 2026-10-31. Using 'on or before' also gives 25.
assumptions: Today is 2026-10-31. 15 stocked lots have no expiry date and are not counted as expired.

answer: There are 43 open purchase order lines.
how_calculated: COUNT(*) over ZV_PURCHASE where ZZSTATUS = 'OPEN'. Every PO has a single item (00010), so lines equal POs. As a check, all 43 have no goods-receipt date, and every RECEIVED line has one.
assumptions: The status column ZZSTATUS defines whether a line is open.

answer: 33 EA of unrestricted stock of material 2119000124: 17 at plant 1120 and 16 at plant 2100.
how_calculated: SUM(LABST) over ZV_STOCK where MATNR = '2119000124'. The 3 rows were also listed one by one (17 + 15 + 1), and all are in the single unit EA.
assumptions: ZV_STOCK is the live table, not the backup or test copy. LABST is unrestricted stock.

how_calculated: COUNT(DISTINCT WERKS) over ZV_PLANT gives 6. The 6 distinct WERKS in ZV_STOCK, ZV_PURCHASE and ZV_REORDER match it.
assumptions: ZV_PLANT is the plant master. The P0-P4 codes in the Z* side tables do not match any master data and are ignored.
